name: xTool D1 Pro
tagline: The most popular open-frame diode laser for makers who outgrow entry-level machines
tldr: A well-built open-frame diode laser available up to 20W. Excellent for engraving wood, leather, and slate. Can cut thin materials but do not expect CO₂-level cutting. The sweet spot for hobbyists who want reliability without CO₂ cost.

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cannot: Clear acrylic cutting (diode light passes through)

pros: Large work area for the price
Strong software support and community tutorials
Good build quality vs. cheaper Chinese diodes
cons: Open frame : you must wear laser safety glasses and supervise operation
20W still cannot match CO₂ for acrylic and thick cuts
Slower on large fill engravings compared to CO₂
Air assist and enclosure sold separately
Diode spot size limits ultra-fine detail vs. fiber/UV
beginnerNotes: The 10W version is enough for most beginners doing engraving and light cutting. Choose 20W if you plan to cut basswood regularly. Always buy proper laser safety glasses rated for your wavelength (~455 nm).
proTips: Use air assist and a honeycomb bed for cleaner cuts. For metal marking, use LaserBond or Brilliance spray : results vary by coating. Upgrade to steel wheel risers if you engrave tumblers or cylindrical objects.
primaryUse: General-purpose hobby engraving on wood, leather, and coated metals, with light cutting of thin wood and dark acrylic.
mainObjective: Hobby engraving on wood, leather & coated metal with light cutting
